why: A cross-compiled ELF or host-rendered screenshot does not prove a usable PS2 client

decision: Keep the pinned PS2DEV build as the reproducible toolchain baseline

decision: Port through the existing gateway contract first

decision: Run PCSX2 only with an isolated virtual display and portable config

decision: Use the user-supplied USA v1.60 BIOS in an isolated portable PCSX2 v2.6.3 profile

decision: Choose a typed scene gateway with PS2-local input, gsKit presentation, and local media playback
why: It preserves canonical console-ui behavior without unsafe R5900 Zig code or a second UI implementation

decision: Use PCSX2 sockets DEV9 with embedded PS2SDK DEV9, NETMAN, and SMAP modules

decision: Serialize canonical Native UI draw commands into a bounded full-scene protocol and replay them with gsKit
why: This retains console-ui semantics while keeping pointers and host ABI details off the wire

decision: Map DualShock pad edges to canonical Native UI actions and return a newly rendered scene
why: The guest sampled Cross through libpad, sent action 2 over DEV9, and transitioned to the home screen
result: VERIFIED live controller and shared UI transition
